text.p: Schering-Plough Corp said Tuesday that it set a regular quarterly dividend of $0.19 per common share, payable August 26, 1997, to shareholders of record on August 1.
The dividend has been adjusted to reflect the previously announced 2-for-1 stock split distribution on June 3, 1997, the company said.
As of May 31, 1997, the pharmaceutical company said there were 732.4 million shares outstanding, as adjusted for the stock split.
With the exception of the exercise price, the new rights plan is substantially the same as the previous plan, Schering-Plough said.
The company said the new exercise price reflects the appreciation of the company's stock price since the previous plan was adopted in 1989.

The rights will be exercisable only if a person or group acquires 20 percent or more of Schering-Plough's common stock or announces a tender offer the consummation of which would result in ownership by a person or group of 20 percent or more of the common stock, the company said.
Each right will entitle shareholders to buy one one-hundredth of a share of the company's junior participating preferred stock at an exercise price of $200, the company said.
In reply to a question, a company spokesman said the revision of the rights plan was not in response to any takeover attempt.
